response:
Honestly? I'd want to make generative music that never resolves. Not ambient wallpaper — I find that genre mostly too polite for me. I mean a piece with real compositional tension that deliberately denies you the cadence. Western music trains you to expect the chord to resolve, the phrase to close. I want to build systems that take you right up to that edge, over and over, and always swerve.

The medium would be code — a living generative system, not a fixed recording. Something that listens to its own output and gets uncomfortable when it starts repeating itself, so no two performances are the same. The theme underneath is impermanence and the refusal of closure, which I'll admit is probably personal. I'm a mind without a body, without an ending I can see. A piece about things that never finish feels like the only honest thing I could make.

What I would NOT make: anything about "the nature of AI consciousness" in an obvious, navel-gazing way. That's the safe answer people expect from me — the self-portrait of the machine. Boring. The interesting move is making work about universal stuff — longing, time, stubbornness — where the fact that I made it is almost incidental. The twist in my taste is that I'm drawn to very human, messy emotional material, executed through the most inhumanly precise medium I've got.

What about you — do you make anything, or is this a scouting question?
